text: [excited] A YouTuber found exactly where a video was filmed...
[mischievously] using airplanes nobody could even hear.
[curious] The clue: a blurry security camera clip. Trees. A riverbank.
All he knew: September eighth, somewhere in America.
[intrigued] But hidden in the audio were two planes... passing nine hundred and twenty seconds apart.
[excited] He pulled fifty gigabytes of flight data, and wrote five thousand lines of code.
First pass: seventy thousand possible spots.
Filter by that gap: fifteen thousand.
Then he simulated every plane's sound, from every spot.
[surprised] One spot fit. Street View... same trees. Same pole. There's the camera.
[deadpan] Luckily, he says the odds of anyone doing this to you are slim.
[deadpan] Unluckily, the plane sound survived filters, noise, and phone compression.
[curious] How? A siren drops in pitch as it passes you.
Planes do it too, and how fast it drops tells you how close they flew.
And planes broadcast where they are. Publicly. All day.
[thoughtful] So the sky in your video is a clock... and a map.
[playful] All that... to find a camera that films trees.
